info.title: halocli surfaced-operations enrichment
info.description: Curated prose for the operations HaloCLI surfaces (registry list/get/create/update/delete plus nested write operations) plus targeted corrections learned from live API testing: POST /Report's array body and failure modes, the loadreport execution parameter, and AnalyzerProfile.sql execution constraints. Applied by scripts/vendor_halo_spec.py with fill-if-missing semantics: upstream text is never overwritten. Target shapes: $.paths[...].<method>.summary|description, $.paths[...].<method>.parameters[?@.name=='<name>'].description, and $.components.schemas.<Schema>.properties.<prop>.description. All three are standard JSONPath (verified against jsonpath-ng in tests), so external overlay runners resolve every action rather than silently skipping some. operationIds are NOT in this file -- they are synthesized deterministically by the vendor script. When the resource registry grows, add actions here until the surfaced-operations test passes.

actions.description: folded from live report-interface testing
actions.update: The body must be a JSON array of AnalyzerProfile: a bare object returns 400 and a non-JSON Content-Type returns 415. Omit id to create a report, include it to update; the stored report is returned.

actions.description: folded from live report-interface testing
actions.update: Execute the report and return the result set under report.rows (read-only GET). Halo returns at most 50,000 rows, so a report over more rows is silently truncated -- bound large reports by date.

actions.description: folded from live report-interface testing
actions.update: Raw T-SQL for a user-authored (type 1) report. Halo executes it inside a derived table, so a trailing ORDER BY is rejected unless the SELECT also specifies TOP or OFFSET (or FOR XML).

actions.update: The spec body is a JSON array of Users (Halo's POST-with-id upsert: omit id to create, include it to update). The spec declares no required fields, but a live create needs at least a username (name), emailaddress, client_id and site_id. Account actions ride the same upsert: resetpassword and new_password for credentials (tenant password policy applies), locked for lockout, and _revoke_authenticatorapp to reset end-user MFA.
